key_insight: Confining Cs2CoCl4 inside single-walled carbon nanotubes drives diameter-dependent 1D polymorphism, producing tetragonal and orthorhombic rod-group structures while largely preserving the Co2+ magnetic state.
engineering_relevance: This shows that nanoscale confinement can be used as a structural design lever to tune metal-halide behavior in 1D architectures without fully changing the underlying magnetic chemistry.
method: Aberration-corrected STEM/TEM imaging of Cs2CoCl4 inside SWCNTs
Multislice simulations to match observed confined structures
DC magnetization fitting to verify Co2+ persistence
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct microscopy plus simulation agreement and magnetic fits showing only a small change in effective moment (4.607(3) to 4.788(3) μB/f.u.) and Weiss constant (-7.9(3) to -4.09(7) K) after confinement.
watch_item: Results depend on extreme 1D confinement inside SWCNTs, so scalability and structural stability outside this nanotube environment remain uncertain.
paper_title: Structural properties of one-dimensional $\mathrm{Cs}_2\mathrm{CoCl}_4$ confined within single-walled carbon nanotubes
